The 45° line through the origin picks out the point where the **magnitudes of u and v
are equal**, and for a lens that happens at 2f.
**Step 1 — see what the 45° line means.** A straight line through the origin at 45° to
the x-axis is the line **|v| = |u|** ✓ Where it crosses the experimental curve, the
object distance and the image distance have the same magnitude.
**Step 2 — impose that condition on the lens equation.** With the real-is-positive
convention, u = −x and v = +x for an object and a real image on opposite sides:
1/v − 1/u = 1/f
1/x + 1/x = 1/f
2/x = 1/f
**x = 2f** ✓
**Step 3 — write the coordinates.** The object distance is plotted as **−2f** and the
image distance as **+2f**, so
**P = (−2f, 2f)** ✓
**Why 2f is the special point.** It is the one position where a convex lens forms an
image the **same size** as the object ✓ The magnification is
m = v/u = 2f/(−2f) = **−1**
real, inverted and life-size - the symmetric configuration of the lens.
**The shape of the rest of the curve.** As the object moves from 2f towards f, the image
runs out towards infinity; as it moves from 2f towards infinity, the image closes in
towards f ✓ The curve is a rectangular hyperbola with asymptotes at u = −f and v = f,
and it is symmetric about the 45° line - which is why that line meets it at exactly one
point.
**A numerical check.** For f = 10 cm, P should be (−20, 20):
1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/10 − 1/20 = 1/20, so **v = 20 cm** ✓ exactly as predicted.
**Why the sign of u is negative.** The object sits on the incoming side of the lens, and
distances measured against the direction of the light are taken as negative ✓ That is
why the correct coordinate pair has one negative and one positive entry.
**Reading the distractors.** **(f, f)** ✗ - an object at f gives an image at infinity,
not at f. **(f/2, f/2)** ✗ - an object inside the focus gives a **virtual** image, and
this point does not lie on the curve. **(4f, 4f)** ✗ - both positive, which no real
object-image pair for a convex lens can be ✓
∴ (−2f, 2f).
